name: web-ingest
title: Chaos: dependencies killed under constant web load
summary: Constant open-model web load (8 events/s, one event per request) against the local single-node Compose stack (project scf-wsl); each dependency killed with SIGKILL for 20 s, then started; finally the gateway itself killed with records in its spool. Availability is judged per second of the load timeline over each outage-and-recovery window; durability by comparing Umami's stored events with the accepted (202) events.

kill umami (the engine) for 20 s: spool drains afterwards

checks.detail: marker page views acknowledged before the kill: 20; spool queued before the kill 51 (fsynced counter 3286); after restart, engine still down: queued gauge 0; after the engine returned: acked_stored 216 vs fsynced since restart 165 (the difference was recovered from disk); marker page views stored in Umami: 20

checks.name: gateway outage with a second edge node (tracker fails over to the other host)
checks.detail: requires: multi-node stack (two edge nodes on two host names); the local stack has one gateway

checks.name: no accepted event lost over the whole run (Umami count ≥ 202 count; any surplus ≤ requests whose answer was lost)
checks.detail: accepted 2303, stored 2325 (surplus 22), transport errors 62 (connections cut by the gateway kill: a request may be fsync'd and forwarded while its 202 never reached the client; event ids are not forwarded to Umami, C-37, so such a surplus cannot be told from a duplicate at this level), statuses {"202":2303,"error":62,"no_proof_ready":72}

checks.name: API path under chaos (Collector queue, writer failover)
checks.detail: requires: otlp (gateway OTLP front door, day 3) and two writers for the failover case (C-77)
